why: Findings from deep-research passes, with verification status as a FIELD rather than a sentence. 'read' means the primary source was retrieved and the figure taken from its own text; 'secondary' means a citing work reported it; 'unread' means believed and unchecked. Paywalls at Nature, ScienceDirect, AIP, ACS and Sandia are why the distinction exists. A measured quantity may seal only as an integer bracket; a convention may seal as an equality.

findings.source: Betz, Zeitschrift fur das gesamte Turbinenwesen 26 (1920) 307-309; English translation Wind Engineering 37 (2013) 441-446
findings.note: Joukowsky co-priority, same year, independent. Exact rational: brackets natively.

findings.note: Exact product, sharper than the commonly quoted 96485.33212.

findings.claim: Methane combustion enthalpy, liquid water basis

findings.note: The project's 890.29 sits at the BOTTOM of the credible band; NIST lists four values spanning 890.3-890.6.

findings.claim: Four-stroke cycle completes in two crankshaft revolutions
findings.source: Runciman, Gas and Oil Engines Simply Explained (Gutenberg 27286); corroborated by Rathbun (Gutenberg 56776)
findings.note: Both books read in full; corroborated independently by the 2:1 camshaft ratio.

findings.claim: One working stroke in four; impulses per revolution equal cylinders divided by two
findings.source: Rathbun, Practical Hand Book of Gas, Oil and Steam Engines (Gutenberg 56776)
findings.note: A firing-frequency fact, NOT an efficiency factor — must not be multiplied into a fuel-energy chain.

findings.claim: No engine book consulted states degrees of crank rotation per stroke or per cycle
findings.source: Runciman 27286, Rathbun 56776, Mathot 38415 — all read in full
findings.note: NEGATIVE RESULT. No 180 degrees, no 720 degrees, and no in-line firing order anywhere. Derivation would have fabricated all three.
